Data Analytics Case Study

Fake Job Posting
Fraud Pattern Detection

An end-to-end analytics project investigating which characteristics of online job postings are associated with fraudulent listings — from SQL cleaning and hypothesis analysis to an interactive Power BI dashboard.

At a glance

The numbers behind the problem

The analysis covers 17,079 job postings and focuses on measurable differences between fraudulent and legitimate listings.

816Fraudulent postings

Evidence, not assumptions

Key findings

Several posting attributes showed notably different fraud rates in the dataset.

01 · COMPANY LOGO

No company logo

16.21%

Fraud rate, compared with 1.83% for postings with a company logo.

02 · EMPLOYMENT TYPE

Part-time roles

9.83%

Fraud rate, compared with 4.09% for full-time postings.

03 · TELECOMMUTING

Remote postings

8.66%

Fraud rate, compared with 4.60% for on-site postings.

04 · SALARY INFORMATION

A counter-intuitive signal

25.12%

Of fraudulent postings listed a salary range, versus 14.87% of genuine postings.

Analytical discipline

Keeping the findings honest

Very small categories can produce misleading percentages. For the industry leaderboard, a minimum threshold of 50 postings per industry was applied. Missing or unlabeled industry values were excluded from the industry ranking because they represent a data-quality gap rather than a real industry.

These results describe associations observed in the dataset. They do not establish that a particular characteristic causes fraudulent behavior.
